chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Nāsib (one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt) was mentioned, so he said: 'Do not marry them, do not eat their slaughtered meat, and do not reside with them.'

As for what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: 'I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) by what a man becomes a Muslim such that his marriage is permissible and his inheritance is valid, and by what his blood becomes protected? He said: 'His blood is protected by Islam when he manifests it, and his marriage and inheritance become permissible.'

So it is not contradictory to what we mentioned earlier, because whoever has enmity and Nusb manifested towards the Family of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) has not truly manifested Islam, but rather is at the peak of manifesting disbelief. And the report only included those who manifested Islam, and these (the Nāsib) are not among those who manifest Islam.

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The Family of the Messenger of Allah (Ahl al-Bayt).
key_terms.النَّاصِبُ: Nāsib: One who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt, often used as a technical term for a specific type of disbeliever in Shia fiqh.
key_terms.تُنَاكِحْهُمْ: To marry them (specifically in the context of permissibility).
key_terms.ذَبِيحَتَهُمْ: Their slaughtered meat (referring to ritual slaughter).
key_terms.يَحْرُمُ دَمُهُ: His blood is protected/protected from being shed (a legal status of a Muslim).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying and eating the meat of the Nāsib in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration to refine the Shia doctrine of *al-Nasb* (enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt), distinguishing between nominal Islam and substantive faith. He argues that while outward profession (*ithar*) generally permits marriage and inheritance, the specific hostility of the *Nāsib* reveals a deeper state of *kufr*, thereby justifying the exclusion of their meat and marital validity despite their outward Muslim status.
